name: Parallel_SSHI_FBR
rationale: The open-circuit voltage of the piezo (~3.8V) is lower than the target output voltage (4.5-5.5V). A standard full-bridge rectifier (FBR) cannot boost this voltage. Parallel SSHI (Synchronized Switch Harvesting on Inductor) uses an inductor and a switch to invert the voltage across the piezo capacitance Cp at its extrema, effectively increasing the voltage swing and boosting the output. I'm using a full-bridge rectifier to capture the energy from both half-cycles and a storage capacitor to filter ripple.

name: SECE_Boost
rationale: Synchronized Electric Charge Extraction (SECE) directly transfers charge from the piezo capacitance to the storage capacitor through an inductor, which can provide significant voltage boosting. This topology uses two paths (one for the positive peak, one for the negative peak) to maximize energy extraction and ensure the output reaches the required 4.5V minimum even under weak excitation (S4).

name: SSHI_HalfBridge
rationale: This is a variation of the SSHI topology using a half-bridge rectifier instead of a full-bridge. In some conditions (like S3 with strong excitation), a full bridge might push Vout above 5.5V. A half-bridge reduces the average current flowing into Cout, which can help keep the voltage within the absolute maximum range while still benefiting from the SSHI voltage boost to meet the minimum supply requirements.
